column1: # THE FLEET, DECLARED. One row per repository in the account.
# WHY A MANIFEST AND NOT "WHATEVER `gh repo list` RETURNS"
# Every gate in this repository checks THIS repository. Nothing checked that the
# fleet as a whole was in the intended state, and the failures that cost the most
# here were all of that shape: a pool pinned off, a lane never armed, a required
# check no workflow emits. Each is invisible from inside the repository it
# affects, because the repository looks exactly like one that is simply idle.
# Discovering the fleet instead of declaring it reproduces that blindness. A new
# repository with no lane and no CI is indistinguishable from a deliberate
# exemption, so a discovery-only audit has to treat it as fine — and the one
# thing worth catching is precisely the repository nobody onboarded. So the
# manifest is the source of truth and `fleet-audit.sh` reports in BOTH
# directions: a row with no repository, and a repository with no row.
# TIERS
#   pool     self-hosted runners in a GCP project, plus the full lane.
#            Audited for pins, arming, required-check agreement AND pool health.
#   lane     the merge lane and its guards, on GitHub-hosted runners.
#            Audited for everything except pool health.
#   checks   CI gates, and deliberately no merge lane: changes land by direct
#            push, so there is no pull request for a lane to gate. The mirror
#            image of `dormant` — audited to confirm the checks are STILL
#            there, because a repository that lost them looks like a quiet one.
#   dormant  no CI at all. Audited to confirm it STILL has no CI: the day
#            somebody adds a workflow, the repository has become a `lane` or a
#            `checks` repository, and that is the finding.
#   empty    no default branch. Nothing to audit until it has one.
#   source   this repository. It calls its own workflows through the `-self`
#            variants rather than pinning a release of itself.
# The reason column is not decoration. An exemption whose reason has gone stale
# is the same defect as a missing gate, and a reason is what makes that
# reviewable a year later.
